angle_en: atyeti: the verb that means to go beyond

en.intro: Krishna points to a single word that marks the limit of all religious action: listen for the verb that means to go beyond.
en.notice: The word is atyeti, meaning goes beyond. The yogi does not merely collect the fruits of sacrifice and austerity; knowing the two paths, he passes beyond them all.
en.next: Krishna now promises to reveal a secret knowledge that frees you from all that is harmful.
en.meaning: Knowing the two paths, the yogi goes beyond all the merits declared in the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and gifts, and reaches the primal supreme abode.

hi.intro: कृष्ण एक ऐसे शब्द की ओर इशारा करते हैं जो सभी धार्मिक कर्मों की सीमा बताता है: उस क्रिया को सुनिए जिसका अर्थ है पार जाना।
hi.meaning: योगी इन दोनों मार्गों को जानकर वेदों, यज्ञों, तपों और दानों में बताए गए सभी पुण्यफलों का अतिक्रमण कर जाता है और आदि स्थान परमात्मा को प्राप्त हो जाता है।
hi.next: गीता का नया अध्याय शुरू होता है।

borrowed: "कृष्ण अब एक गुप्त ज्ञान देने वाले हैं जो तुम्हें हर तरह के हानिकारक से मुक्त कर देगा।" (The 'next' field for the Hindi script borrows the content of the NEXT verse (verse 1 of chapter 9). The source specifies that the next verse is the beginning of chapter 9, not the conclusion of this verse (28), and the content of verse 1 is about revealing secret knowledge, which is not part of verse 28.)

meaning_changed: "योगी इन दोनों मार्गों को जानकर वेदों, यज्ञों, तपों और दानों में बताए गए सभी पुण्यफलों का अतिक्रमण कर जाता है और आदि स्थान परमात्मा को प्राप्त हो जाता है।" (The Hindi translation omits the crucial phrase 'विदित्वा' (having known the two paths) at the beginning, which is the cause for the yogi's transcendence in the original Sanskrit. The English meaning clearly states 'Knowing the two paths', but the Hindi translation presents it as a simple conjunction of two actions rather than a conditional/causal relationship.)
